intended_object: The canonical isomorphism U_{σ×τ} ≅ U_σ ×_{Spec ℂ} U_τ, which identifies the affine toric variety of a product cone (in the product lattice N × N') with the fibre product over Spec ℂ of the affine toric varieties of the two factor cones (Fulton §1.4; Cox–Little–Schenck §1.2). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
In this library, `affineToricScheme hi σ` is Spec of the semigroup algebra ℂ[σ^∨ ∩ M]. The isomorphism is built in two steps. First, Spec is applied to the ℂ-algebra isomorphism ℂ[S_σ] ⊗_ℂ ℂ[S_τ] ≅ ℂ[S_{σ×τ}]. That isomorphism comes from (σ×τ)^∨ ∩ (M×M') ≅ (σ^∨ ∩ M) × (τ^∨ ∩ M') together with ℂ[G×H] ≅ ℂ[G] ⊗ ℂ[H]. Second, it is composed with Mathlib's `pullbackSpecIso`, which identifies Spec(A ⊗_ℂ B) with the pullback Spec A ×_{Spec ℂ} Spec B. This is the standard proof that affine toric varieties of product cones are products.

The lemmas that follow (`affineToricSchemeProdIso_hom_fst` and `_hom_snd`) show that the two projections are the toric morphisms induced by the lattice projections. So this is the canonical isomorphism, not an arbitrary one.

Working over ℂ and taking the lattices in `Type` (needed so the universes match `Spec ℂ`) are conventions fixed by the library's definition of `affineToricScheme`. They are not extra restrictions of this declaration, and working over ℂ is the standard setting of Fulton and CLS. Mathlib has no toric-variety counterpart.
